title: How can a compass mark points four centimetres from P?
description: A compass is opened against a ruler until its tip and pencil are four centimetres apart. The tip is fixed on P and only the pencil moves, so every point it marks is four centimetres from P. Keeko raises the doubt about opening the compass to two centimetres.
teaching_notes: One idea: the gap between the compass tip and the pencil is the distance of every point from P. Watch for children who open the compass to half the width they want.

source: You can start by marking a few points of distance 4 cm from P using the compass. How can this be done?
video_script.why: The child sets the compass against a ruler and sees that the gap between tip and pencil is the distance from P.
video_script.substitution: Open the compass against a ruler, fix the tip on P and swing the pencil.
video_script.anchor: A compass opened beside a ruler, with the point P marked on the page
video_script.wrong_answer: open the compass to two centimetres
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko opens the compass to two centimetres so that the circle is four centimetres wide. Every point is then only two centimetres from P.
video_script.payoff_line: Every point the pencil marks is four centimetres from P.

final_answer.value: open the compass to 4 cm against a ruler, fix the tip at P and swing the pencil to get a full circle
final_answer.spoken: open the compass to four centimetres against a ruler, fix the tip at P and swing the pencil all the way round

maths_rules: Gap between the tip and the pencil = 4 cm = distance of every marked point from P.
Slip: a gap of 2 cm gives points 2 cm from P, which make a circle 2 cm + 2 cm = 4 cm wide.
The tip stays on P and only the pencil moves.
video_script.design: One idea: the opening of the compass is the distance from P. Assumes a ruler and the page with P. Wrong idea: open to half the distance. The compass stays all video.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko wants to open the compass to two centimetres, so that the circle is four centimetres wide.

<bookmark mark='strike'/>The gap between the tip and the pencil is the distance from P.
That gap must be four centimetres.
